note: Popov-Chang syndrome involves YWHAZ (encoding 14-3-3 zeta), a paralog of YWHAE (involved in Miller-Dieker syndrome 17p13.3 microdeletions characterized by classic lissencephaly and congenital heart defects); distinguishing them clinically by the absence of lissencephaly/congenital heart defects in YWHAZ is plausible.

evidence.text: Miller-Dieker syndrome (MDS) involves deletion of genes on chromosome 17p13.3 including YWHAE and PAFAH1B1, presenting with hallmark classic lissencephaly, abnormal neuronal migration, and congenital heart defects.

source.title: Understanding the Molecular Basis of Miller–Dieker Syndrome
source.quote: Miller-Dieker Syndrome (MDS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a heterozygous deletion of approximately 26 genes within the MDS locus of human chromosome 17. MDS, which affects 1 in 100,000 babies, can lead to a range of phenotypes, including lissencephaly, severe neurological defects, distinctive facial abnormalities, cognitive impairments, seizures, growth retardation, and congenital heart and liver abnormalities.

evidence.text: Miller-Dieker syndrome is characterized by lissencephaly, altered facial features, seizures, and congenital heart disease.

source.title: Miller-Dieker syndrome - Genetics
source.quote: Children with MDS are often born with associated end-organ involvement including congenital heart disease as well as motor and neurologic impairments including seizures.
